This build isn’t connected to a PhotoDuel server.

PhotoDuel is for small groups of friends. Share photos you took yourself and that fit the prompt.

Don’t post nudity, violence, hate, or photos of people who didn’t agree to be in them. Don’t harass or bully anyone.

If something feels wrong, report the photo or the person from the menu next to it. Reports are reviewed, and the person you report isn’t told who reported them. You can also block someone: you won’t see each other’s photos and can’t vote for each other.

A photo reported by 3 different people is hidden until it has been reviewed.

PhotoDuel doesn’t ask for your email, phone number or real name. Your account is a guest account with the name you chose.

Before a photo leaves your phone, the app resizes it and removes location and camera details. The server does the same again.

Only members of a room can see its photos, and only after voting opens. Photos are deleted 30 days after a challenge ends, and within 24 hours when a challenge is cancelled or a room is deleted.

Deleting your account removes your photos at once and takes you out of every room. Votes you cast stay counted without your name.

Everyone on the player list submits one photo. You can replace or withdraw it until submissions close.

When submissions close, each player votes once for a photo that isn’t their own. Votes are secret and can’t be changed.

When voting closes, the server counts the votes. The photo with the most votes wins. If photos share the most votes, they all win: there is no hidden tie-break.

If fewer than 2 photos were submitted, or fewer than 2 votes were counted, there is no winner. Deadlines come from the server’s clock, not your phone’s.
